resolvedQuestions: The forks have different telemetry durability and lifecycle boundaries.
The two extensions have an explicit DeepSeek ownership exclusion contract.
Test coverage is modular in deep-pi and concentrated in pi-cache-optimizer.
DeepPi needs explicit cold-write, malformed-number, and retry fixtures.
The FakePi harness cannot prove non-interactive report transport.
The optimizer lacks production lifecycle coverage for message_end accounting and persisted stats.
No combined-host test enforces one owner across both extensions.
The declared DeepPi live benchmark entry point is absent.
DeepPi omits maintained storm and stability counters from its report.
Both command reports are text-only and lack a versioned machine-readable contract.
Optimizer recent samples are in-memory while aggregate stats persist.
Persistence failure state is transient and not durable/reportable.
DeepPi mixes observed Pi cost with a separate rate-based savings estimate.
Optimizer stats are token-only unless an explicit pricing layer is added.
The two forks use different cache metric denominators.
No controlled cold/warm or extension-overhead benchmark path exists.
Optimizer provider, persistence, and lifecycle concerns are coupled in one large entry module.
DeepPi modules are separated but root reset/report wiring is manual.
Ownership needs a first-class matrix and combined-host contract test.
Vendored fork provenance and synchronization are manual.
Current guard and basic load/regression paths are already accepted by sibling packets.
Remaining live gaps are explicit verification boundaries, not proof that local code paths are absent.
Correctness and contracts must precede report, persistence, economics, extraction, and provenance work.

keyFindings.title: DeepPi telemetry is process-local
keyFindings.summary: DeepPi resets in-memory telemetry per session and exposes reports through the UI notify channel; the optimizer has versioned persistent session and total buckets.

keyFindings.title: DeepSeek ownership is explicit
keyFindings.summary: The optimizer returns before its hooks for the two DeepPi-owned direct model IDs, while DeepPi gates its own transforms on the same direct provider and ID predicate.

keyFindings.title: Test layout is asymmetric
keyFindings.summary: DeepPi has focused module and integration suites; the optimizer concentrates review coverage in one large suite despite an 8,390-line entry module.

keyFindings.title: Share contracts before code
keyFindings.summary: The forks share telemetry concepts but differ in provider and routing scope, so a common schema and ownership test is safer than forced implementation sharing.

keyFindings.title: DeepPi drops pure cache-write usage
keyFindings.summary: The recorder rejects input=0/cacheRead=0 even when cacheWrite is positive, and its counters exclude cacheWrite from miss tokens, denominator, and input cost.

keyFindings.title: DeepPi lacks failed-attempt filtering
keyFindings.summary: DeepPi records matching message_end usage without a stopReason guard; the optimizer skips error and aborted messages to avoid retry inflation.

keyFindings.title: Ownership lists can drift
keyFindings.summary: DeepPi eligibility and optimizer ownership each hardcode the same two direct model IDs, creating a double-processing risk when support changes.

keyFindings.title: DeepPi trusts numeric usage values
keyFindings.summary: DeepPi mutates counters without finite/nonnegative validation, while optimizer normalization rejects malformed numeric fields and tracks missing samples.

keyFindings.title: DeepPi lacks boundary telemetry fixtures
keyFindings.summary: Current tests do not cover pure cache writes, malformed numeric usage, or failed and aborted usage-bearing message_end events.

keyFindings.title: FakePi cannot prove non-interactive report transport
keyFindings.summary: The test harness records UI notifications but has no RPC, stdout, or structured command channel for the full /deeppi report.

keyFindings.title: Optimizer production accounting lifecycle is untested end to end
keyFindings.summary: The optimizer suite does not emit message_end events through persistence and restart, so production hook wiring is not proven by the current tests.

keyFindings.title: No combined-host coexistence contract test
keyFindings.summary: The two suites load their extensions separately and do not prove one-owner behavior when both are registered in the same Pi host.

keyFindings.title: Declared DeepPi live benchmark entry point is absent
keyFindings.summary: benchmark:live points at scripts/live-benchmark.mjs, but that file is absent and the existence check exits 1.

keyFindings.title: DeepPi report omits maintained storm and stability counters
keyFindings.summary: errorsEnhanced, prunedThinking, and preservedThinking are maintained but not passed into the /deeppi report.

keyFindings.title: Both command reports lack a versioned machine-readable contract
keyFindings.summary: DeepPi and optimizer commands return human-formatted strings through ctx.ui.notify without a shared schemaVersion or JSON projection.

keyFindings.title: Optimizer trend samples are not persisted across restart
keyFindings.summary: The optimizer retains up to 50 numeric recent samples in memory while persisted files store aggregate buckets only, so restart loses trend and missing-field evidence.

keyFindings.title: Optimizer persistence failures are not durable reportable health state
keyFindings.summary: Write failures trigger logs and a one-time warning, but no last-success, failure-count, or memory-only status survives or appears in stats.

keyFindings.title: DeepPi mixes observed cost with a separate rate-based savings estimate
keyFindings.summary: Actual input cost uses Pi usage.cost while estimated savings uses model rates and omits output/cache-write economics or reconciliation.

keyFindings.title: Optimizer economics are token-only without optional pricing
keyFindings.summary: Persisted optimizer stats retain token counts and ratios but no price metadata or dollar-savings field, appropriately avoiding unsupported proxy assumptions.

keyFindings.title: Fork headline cache metrics use different denominators
keyFindings.summary: DeepPi's token hit rate excludes cache writes while optimizer total input includes them and also exposes request and token ratios, so headline percentages are not directly equivalent.

keyFindings.title: No controlled cold-warm or extension-overhead benchmark exists
keyFindings.summary: The code records sample timestamps but no duration; the declared DeepPi benchmark entry point is absent and prior live evidence was one-request or partial-observability evidence.

keyFindings.title: Optimizer entry module couples unrelated contracts
keyFindings.summary: The 8,390-line entrypoint contains prompt transforms, provider adapters, normalizers, persistence, routing, diagnostics, commands, and hooks, with a broad test-only export.

keyFindings.title: DeepPi root reset and report wiring is manually maintained
keyFindings.summary: The modular fork's root entrypoint manually resets subsystem fields and chooses report inputs, allowing maintained counters to be omitted.

keyFindings.title: Ownership lacks a first-class contract artifact
keyFindings.summary: DeepPi exports the model list but optimizer repeats literal IDs; no generated matrix or combined-host test forces future edits to update both.

keyFindings.title: Vendored provenance and synchronization are manual
keyFindings.summary: Sibling packets document byte-identical vendored copies with no automatic synchronization or source-drift guard.

keyFindings.title: Sibling acceptance proves the current guard boundary but not future ownership changes
keyFindings.summary: Prior packets already prove current guard, non-DeepSeek regressions, and basic DeepPi load paths; combined-host, future-ID, cold-write, retry, and report serialization remain unproven.

keyFindings.title: Remaining live gaps are explicit verification boundaries
keyFindings.summary: RPC report body, an unavailable opencode credential, and the missing benchmark entry point are blocked prerequisites; local formatter and provider tests do not establish real host behavior.

keyFindings.title: Correctness-gated staged order is supported by the evidence
keyFindings.summary: Deterministic accounting and ownership fixtures should precede report/persistence contracts, then pricing/benchmarking, then broad extraction and provenance automation.

ruledOutDirections.direction: Treating both extensions as interchangeable implementations
ruledOutDirections.reason: Their provider and routing scopes differ.

ruledOutDirections.direction: Treating DeepPi's current in-memory report as persistent observability
ruledOutDirections.reason: Session reset and no filesystem state.
Existing suites cover atomic replacement, snapshot races, symlink safety, collisions, overlapping edits, and mixed message ordering.

ruledOutDirections.direction: Treating FakePi notification capture as non-interactive report proof
ruledOutDirections.reason: The harness has no RPC/stdout channel.

ruledOutDirections.direction: Persisting raw messages or provider payloads
ruledOutDirections.reason: Numeric-only samples provide diagnosis without sensitive content.
A shared versioned report object should precede text or JSON projections.

ruledOutDirections.direction: Inferring dollar prices from model names or adapter families
ruledOutDirections.reason: Pricing and routing are external configuration.

ruledOutDirections.direction: Replacing provider-reported costs with a local estimate
ruledOutDirections.reason: Observed cost and counterfactual estimates serve different purposes.

ruledOutDirections.direction: A full optimizer rewrite as the first step
ruledOutDirections.reason: Narrow extraction and lifecycle/contract tests have lower risk and higher evidence value.

ruledOutDirections.direction: Merging DeepPi and optimizer into one implementation
ruledOutDirections.reason: Provider scope, transforms, retry controls, and persistence contracts differ.

ruledOutDirections.direction: Repeating the already-proven current two-model guard smoke test as the primary next step
ruledOutDirections.reason: Sibling packets contain acceptance receipts for that path.

ruledOutDirections.direction: Treating blocked live prerequisites as resolved evidence
ruledOutDirections.reason: Credential and RPC limitations are explicitly recorded.

iterationFindings.focus: Correctness boundaries in usage, eligibility, and retries

activeRisks: Live provider checks may remain blocked by missing credentials.
The four limitations in the research brief are accepted baseline context, not new findings.
Pure cache-write accounting and failed-attempt filtering need explicit regression fixtures.
Non-interactive report transport remains a host-level verification gap.
The declared benchmark command cannot produce live evidence until its entry point and credential contract are resolved.
Current reports cannot be consumed reliably by non-interactive automation without an explicit schema.
A persistence failure can be visible only in the current process until durable health state exists.
Cross-fork cache percentages cannot be compared without an explicit denominator contract.
No live performance claim is supported until the benchmark entry point and controlled replay are available.
Manual source drift can make the vendored operational copy diverge from upstream provenance.
Root-level wiring can omit new subsystem state unless report/reset contracts are made explicit.
Live host transport, credentials, and benchmark execution remain external follow-up prerequisites.
Implementation has not been performed in this research lineage by design.
